---
title: "Listings"
description: "Generate lists of pages or hand-written entries with `listing:`."
---

## Contents

`contents:` names what a listing shows. Each entry is either a glob that
selects project documents, or an inline record — a small map that *is* an
item.

### Globs

A glob resolves against the file it is written in — the listing page's
own directory for front-matter patterns, the directory holding a
`_metadata.yml`, or the project root for patterns in `_quarto.yml`. `*`
matches one directory level; use `**/` or name a directory to search
subdirectories. A leading `/` anchors at the project root from anywhere.
See [`Q-12-19`](/errors/listing/Q-12-19.qmd) for the full rules and the
common ways a pattern matches nothing.

### Records

```yaml
listing:
  id: cards
  type: grid
  contents:
    - title: "Get started"
      description: "Download and install"
      image: images/rocket.png
    - title: "Release notes"
      path: https://example.com/releases
```

A record's `title`, `subtitle`, `description`, `author`, `date`,
`date-modified`, `image`, `image-alt`, `categories`, `order`, `path`,
`reading-time-minutes` and `word-count` (and other fields besides) are the
same fields a document supplies. Any other key becomes a custom field a
custom template can read as `$item.key$` (also `$item.extra.key$`) — which
also makes a misspelled field name easy to miss, since it's kept rather
than rejected; watch for [`Q-12-22`](/errors/listing/Q-12-22.qmd) if an
item is missing a field you thought you set. A record needs a `title:` or
a `path:` to render meaningfully — one with neither produces an
empty-titled item ([`Q-12-21`](/errors/listing/Q-12-21.qmd)). Relative
`image:` and `path:` values resolve against the file the listing is
written in.

### Records that point at a document

`path: guide/install.qmd` merges the record over that document's own
entry: the record's fields win, the document supplies the rest (link,
description, date, …). A `path:` that is an external URL or a
non-document file is used as the link as written. A `path:` that looks
like a document (has a `.qmd`/`.md`/`.Rmd`/`.ipynb` extension) but names
one the project doesn't render — a typo, or a file outside
`project.render` — builds the item from the record's own fields alone
and keeps the link as written, and warns
([`Q-12-20`](/errors/listing/Q-12-20.qmd)).

### Order

Items are sorted by the listing's `sort:`. **With no `sort:` key, the
default is `order asc, title asc`** — since records usually carry neither
an `order:` nor a `date:`, this alphabetizes a hand-curated `contents:`
list by title. To keep a curated list in the order you wrote it, set
`sort: false`, or give each record an explicit `order:`.

With `sort: false`, items appear in the order of the `contents:` entries
— records included — with one exception: when `contents:` holds only
negated patterns (e.g. `["!draft.qmd", {title: Featured}]`), the implicit
"everything else" positive counts as declared before every entry, so a
record sorts after those items no matter where it's written. (Quarto 1
placed all records after all glob matches.)

### Not yet supported

YAML files in `contents:` (Quarto 1's `contents: items.yml`) are skipped
with a warning ([`Q-12-23`](/errors/listing/Q-12-23.qmd)); move the
records inline.
